_comment: What the nightly update check (home/dot_local/bin/update-check, #550) watches. One entry per flake input, one rolling PR per entry (branch update/<input>). follow = branch: the input tracks a branch and `nix flake update <input>` moves it. follow = release: flake.nix pins a tag or a commit, and the check moves the pin to the newest stable GitHub release. versions are flake attribute paths read before and after; notes name the GitHub releases whose bodies go into the PR for the version range. hosts are the closures the gate builds; build names any further flake output it builds (a package no host enables yet). switch is what a switch to the bump restarts, written for Tom. Adding a program is an edit here. The clock is a routine on the substrate floor (substrate T-7); nothing in this repo schedules it. issues watches report new upstream kernel series without changing the selected series; kernel compares major.minor only and ignores release candidates.

inputs.name: llm-agents
inputs.switch: Home Manager only. Running agent sessions keep the binary they started with; the next session starts on the new one. The substrate units find claude and codex through the profile, so their unit text does not change and nothing restarts. dsh is the pkgs/dsh wrapper around llm-agents.dsh; its policy is store --patch overlays, so a bump changes nothing under ~/.dsh, and checks.dsh-config (built above) re-checks the policy against the new release. checks.dsh-plugins (built above) re-runs the herdr profile's plugin tests against the new dsh-tools and boots that profile; its plugins are re-linked under ~/.dsh/profiles/herdr only when Tom next runs `dsh herdr`.

inputs.name: herdr
inputs.switch: The herdr server keeps X-SwitchMethod=keep-old, so a switch never kills a live PTY. The new server runs only after a deliberate `systemctl --user restart herdr`, and existing clients need a new projector launch.

inputs.name: gufo-rdma
inputs.switch: Tracks neuhaus/gufo branch rdma. Only the on-demand gufo-tp2.service uses this build; no boot target. The upstream gufo input and single-box :8731 unit stay pinned until hardware qualification. Starting TP2 conflicts with the single-box text/image units. Model revisions remain a separate Library declaration.

inputs.name: donnerkeule
inputs.switch: Tracks mecattaf/donnerkeule codex/framework-7-3. Updates the module and matching usb4_rdma provider on both compute hosts. Stage/reboot both onto the same kernel and rerun the attended rail/throughput qualification before TP2 use. Never reload or reboot from the update routine.

inputs.name: vicinae
inputs.switch: Client only, through `deploy .#client`. The Vicinae user service restarts in the Sway session.

inputs.name: nixpkgs-fresh
inputs.switch: A new kernel is only staged: it runs after the next reboot, which stays Tom's to name. Chrome on the client updates with `deploy .#client`; an open browser keeps its running version until it is closed by its user. Tailscale follows this fresh input on the NAS, client and coordinator; the worker has no Tailscale service. A Tailscale bump changes tailscaled's unit and can restart the network transport, so leave that candidate staged whenever activation would interrupt a connection or session. The NAS takes this only on a NAS deploy, which is a decision.

issues.name: linux
issues.reason: This is a new stable major.minor series, not a point release. The fleet currently selects its kernel from nixpkgs-fresh. Kernel-series adoption and reboot are explicit daytime decisions; this watcher changes neither.
